method: closes split-adjusted, not dividend-adjusted (price returns); 52 weeks = sessions after the same day a year earlier; volatility = sample sd of daily log returns x sqrt(252) (365 for a 7-day market); beta = OLS slope vs ^GSPC: b5 60 completed monthly returns (Yahoo's method), b1 252 daily returns on common sessions

keys.since: first session when the history is younger than 52 weeks (the range is since then)
keys.ppy: observations per year when not 252 (365 = a 7-day market)
keys.b5: [beta vs ^GSPC, 60 completed monthly returns (Yahoo's method), n, R^2]
keys.dd: [largest peak-to-trough fall % inside the 52 weeks, peak date, trough date]
keys.q: flags: stale · short · jump:<date>:x<ratio> · px:x<ratio> (our last close vs the book's for that session)
keys.u52: 1 = the closing range may fill a blank 52-week high / low
keys.x52: Yahoo's 52-week range is wrong - show ours: 1 = a close outside it, 2 = its extreme a split factor beyond every close
keys.w52: 1 = Yahoo's 52-week extreme is 25 %+ beyond every close: show both
keys.ub: [beta, 'm' monthly | 'd' daily] that may fill a blank beta (US-listed USD equities / ETFs)
